engagement.coverage_declaration: Full audit. Web API: handlers/auth.go, handlers/login.go, handlers/validate.go, handlers/logout.go, pkg/cookie/cookie.go, pkg/jwtmanager/jwtmanager.go, pkg/cfg/cfg.go, pkg/providers/* (all OAuth provider implementations); Supply chain: go.mod/go.sum, .github/workflows/* (5 actions), Dockerfile/Dockerfile.alpine, do.sh build scripts; Infrastructure: TLS config, session management, secret generation. Not analyzed: .git history (per instructions), nested dependencies' CVEs (requires govulncheck tool not available), runtime behavior of upstream OAuth providers, post-deployment operational security (log retention, perimeter network, IDP hardening).
engagement.authorization: Local code review only; no network testing, no credentials used, no remote services probed.

OAuth tokens forwarded to downstream headers

Session key validation is soft (warnings only)

dropped.reason: URL validated against domain allow-list before session storage; Go's url.Parse handles @-confusion correctly.

inventoried: Go 1.25 project (golang-jwt v5, oauth2 v0.36, Gorilla sessions)
OAuth/OIDC proxy for Nginx auth_request (9 providers: Google, GitHub, Azure, Okta, Slack, Discord, Nextcloud, Alibaba, OpenStax)
Gorilla CookieStore sessions with optional PKCE
JWT with configurable signing (HS256/RS256/ES256), optional gzip compression
5 GitHub Actions workflows (coverage, docker releases × 3, IRC notify)
not_read: templates/, static/ (web assets, assumed safe by template/html)

findings.title: Attacker-chosen cookie names cause unbounded allocation and panics (CWE-789, CWE-129)
findings.evidence: Lines 117–137 parse multipart cookies (VouchCookie_1of2, etc.) without bounds checking. Attacker sends VouchCookie_1of100000000=payload. Line 130: make([]string, 1e8) allocates 1.6 GB. Or VouchCookie_x=1 causes panic on xyArray[1]. Reachable from any internet user via /validate before authentication.
findings.impact: Unauthenticated denial of service. A handful of crafted HTTP requests OOM-kills Vouch and every site behind it, or panic-abort connections.
findings.preconditions: vouch.cookie.name configured (default VouchCookie); Nginx forwards client Cookie headers to /validate (standard config).
findings.recommendation: Bounds-check part count and index: reject if numParts<1 or >32, reject if index<1 or >numParts. Use io.LimitReader on cookie size.
findings.verification: Send request with Cookie: VouchCookie_1of1000000000=x; verify no allocation panic; send request with Cookie: VouchCookie_9of2=x and verify no index panic.
traceability: CWE-789: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value
CWE-129: Improper Validation of Array Index
CWE-248: Uncaught Exception (panic recovery)
OWASP A05:2021: Denial of Service

triage.reason: Cookie name and part count are entirely attacker-controlled via HTTP header.
make([]string, N) does allocate memory; this is not a non-dangerous sink.
Boundary crossed: attacker (internet) → application process → OS memory.

findings.limits: Panic is per-connection (recovered by net/http); allocation variant is process-global and is not recovered.

findings.title: Unauthenticated gzip decompression bomb before signature verification (CWE-409, CWE-400)
findings.evidence: Lines 140–143: gzip decompression happens before JWT signature check. Function decodeAndDecompressTokenString (lines 188–207) calls io.ReadAll(zr) with no limit. Attacker sends GET /validate?access_token=base64url(gzip(770MB of zeros)). No size check, no io.LimitReader.
findings.impact: Unauthenticated denial of service via compression bomb. Go's default MaxHeaderBytes is 1 MB; gzip ratio is ~1032:1 → 1 MB input → ~1 GB heap per request. Multi-part cookies (each cookie is separate header) let attacker fill budget from cookie header alone. OOMs the process.
findings.preconditions: jwt.compress: true (default in .defaults.yml:31). JWT accepted from query string, header, or cookie (FindJWT accepts all four sources).
findings.recommendation: Wrap gzip reader in io.LimitReader(zr, 1<<20+1); if decompressed size exceeds 1 MB, return error. Also verify CRC by checking zr.Close() error after ReadAll.
findings.verification: Send POST /validate with X-Vouch-Token=base64url(gzip(10 MB zeros)); verify function returns error and does not allocate; measure heap before/after.
traceability: CWE-409: Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data
CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption ('Resource Exhaustion')
OWASP A05:2021: Denial of Service

triage.reason: Compressed payload is attacker-controlled; query string, header, and cookie are all unauthenticated inputs.
io.ReadAll reads all bytes up to EOF; no built-in limit.

findings.limits: Requires compressed input; an uncompressed 1 MB JWT would also cause heap contention but is less efficient for attacker.

findings.title: Azure identity derived from unvalidated token with no tenant/audience binding (CWE-347, CWE-290)
findings.evidence: Lines 52–95 base64-decode the JWT payload and unmarshal into structs.AzureUser without verifying the signature, iss, aud, exp, or tid. No JWKS fetch, no tenant binding. config/config.yml_example_azure:18-19 leaves tenant as '...' (multi-tenant enabled). If multi-tenant, attacker registers victim@managed-domain.com in their own Entra tenant, signs in, and is authorized into the managed domain via email domain check.
findings.impact: Authentication bypass in multi-tenant Azure deployments. Attacker from any Entra tenant can claim to be anyone@managed-domain.com and gain access.
findings.preconditions: Azure tenant configured as multi-tenant or using access_token as identity source (default: access_token, which is unsupported by Microsoft).
findings.recommendation: Switch to ID token. Verify with JWKS: jwt.WithIssuer(config), jwt.WithAudience(cfg.GenOAuth.ClientID), jwt.WithExpirationRequired(), jwt.WithValidMethods([]string{"RS256"}). Enforce explicit tid allow-list. Validate nonce against session.
findings.verification: Deploy with multi-tenant config; attempt login with a user from an attacker-controlled Entra tenant matching the domain; verify rejection.
traceability: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
CWE-290: Authentication Bypass by Spoofing
OWASP A07:2021: Identification and Authentication Failures

triage.reason: No compensating control ties token to tenant.
Token claims are attacker-controlled (attacker controls their own IdP claims).

findings.title: email_verified flag parsed and discarded by all providers; unverified email authorizes (CWE-345)
findings.evidence: Field declared at line 88, never read. Eleven provider implementations (discord.go:82, openid.go:57, google.go:57, github.go, nextcloud.go:64, alibaba.go:64, adfs.go:125, openstax.go:42, indieauth.go, homeassistant.go) unmarshal email_verified then ignore it. handlers/auth.go:164-169 authorizes on email domain via IsUnderManagement() without checking the flag.
findings.impact: Authorization bypass. Against any IdP allowing self-asserted email (generic OIDC, self-hosted Nextcloud, Discord), attacker registers attacker@managed-domain.com and is authorized into every site behind Vouch.
findings.preconditions: Domain-based authorization configured (default); IdP does not enforce email verification.
findings.recommendation: Add EmailVerified bool to structs.User. In verifyUser() Domains branch, reject when flag is false or absent (configurable, default strict). Gate discord.go line 82 on dUser.Verified.
findings.verification: Deploy against a self-hosted Nextcloud; register unverified email matching managed domain; attempt login and verify rejection.
traceability: CWE-345: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity
OWASP A04:2021: Insecure Design
OIDC Core §5.7

triage.reason: Email claim is IdP-supplied and not user-input, but IdP does not verify it.

findings.title: Release Dockerfiles discard all dependency pinning (go get -u ./...)
findings.evidence: Line 18: RUN ./do.sh goget. do.sh:112-116: go get -u -v ./... upgrades every dependency to latest and rewrites go.mod/go.sum. Every published image (quay.io/vouch/vouch-proxy, docker.io/voucher/vouch-proxy) discards checksum guarantees at build time. No commit history reflects the change; it is invisible to audit.
findings.impact: Supply-chain compromise. Attacker who compromises any of ~30 transitive dependencies publishes a malicious patch release; the next master push silently includes it. High-value targets: theckman/go-securerandom (generates JWT secret, session key) and nirasan/go-oauth-pkce-code-verifier (untagged 2022 pseudo-version, on PKCE path).
findings.preconditions: A transitive dependency is compromised or typosquatted.
findings.recommendation: Remove goget from both Dockerfiles. Use RUN go mod download && go mod verify with committed manifests. Both crypto libraries are ~30 lines of wrapping crypto/rand; consider inlining to remove the exposure.
findings.verification: Audit a released image: docker inspect vouch:latest-arm | grep -i go, or extract layers and check go.mod timestamp/content versus commit date.
traceability: CWE-1357: Reliance on Uncontrolled Component
OWASP A08:2021: Software and Data Integrity Failures
SLSA Build L0 (failed: deps not pinned at build time)

triage.reason: No external policy controls the upgrade; it happens inside the Dockerfile.

findings.title: Mutable tags in GitHub Actions workflows holding registry credentials (CWE-829)
findings.evidence: Intended pins: docker/login-action@f054a8b5, docker/metadata-action@a67f45cb, docker/build-push-action@ad44023a (SHA pinned). But same jobs use: actions/checkout@v2, docker/setup-qemu-action@v3, docker/setup-buildx-action@v3, crazy-max/ghaction-docker-buildx@v1 (all mutable tags). A retagged v2/v3 at the action's repo means compromised step in the sequence holding QUAYIO_ROBOT_PASSWORD and DOCKER_PASSWORD.
findings.impact: Registry credential theft. Attacker who controls the action repo (or a maintainer account) injects a step to ex-filtrate credentials and push trojaned images to quay.io and docker.io.
findings.preconditions: Maintainer or action repo is compromised.
findings.recommendation: Pin every uses: to full 40-char SHA with # vX.Y.Z comment. Replace deprecated buildx action. Add .github/dependabot.yml with package-ecosystem: github-actions.
findings.verification: Run gh workflow view -r <repo> and grep 'uses:'; count mutable vs pinned; cross-check SHAs against GitHub API.
traceability: CWE-829: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
OWASP A08:2021: Software and Data Integrity Failures
SLSA Build L2 failed (actions not pinned by digest)

triage.reason: No external policy enforces action pinning; the workflows control their own inputs.

findings.title: /validate authorization cached without the Host header as key (CWE-524)
findings.evidence: Lines 54–72 cache JWT validation results by JWT alone. ValidateRequestHandler (validate.go:54-60) gates on r.Host: domains.Matches(r.Host) must not be empty. But cache bypass on line 57 returns immediately on cache hit without re-checking Host. Attacker forges Host header or performs DNS rebind; subsequent request with same JWT but unmanaged Host bypasses domain check.
findings.impact: Authorization bypass via Host spoofing. An attacker who can spoof/control the Host header (HTTP/1.1 request, DNS rebind, proxy misconfiguration) accesses an unmanaged backend that should have been refused.
findings.preconditions: Host-based routing used (common); attacker can spoof or control Host header.
findings.recommendation: Key cache on jwt + "\x00" + r.Host. Or: re-check Host on cache-hit path before returning 200.
findings.verification: Send valid JWT with Host: attacker.com; verify rejection; send same JWT with Host: managed-domain.com; verify first caches it; send again with Host: attacker.com and verify it now bypasses the check.
traceability: CWE-524: Use of Cache Containing Sensitive Information
CWE-863: Incorrect Authorization

triage.reason: No compensating control enforces Host check on cache-hit path.

findings.title: Expired JWT cached indefinitely if expiration time crosses current second (CWE-613)
findings.evidence: getCacheExpirationDuration (lines 91-112) returns Duration based on token.ExpiresAt.Unix() - now.Unix(). If d == 0 (expires within current second), go-cache treats it as DefaultExpiration (20 minutes) and caches the expired token. If d < 0 (GC pause between verification and this line), go-cache.Set ignores Expiration == 0 and never expires the entry — it lives until process restart.
findings.impact: Privilege escalation via cache poisoning. A token that is only expired by milliseconds (or during a GC pause) is cached as valid for 20 minutes (or indefinitely). An attacker with a token about to expire can exploit the race window.
findings.preconditions: Token's ExpiresAt is very close to current time (< 1 second); or a GC pause occurs between token verification and cache TTL calculation.
findings.recommendation: ttl := time.Until(claims.ExpiresAt.Time); if ttl <= 0 { return 0 }; if ttl > dExp { ttl = dExp }; return ttl. Caller must skip Cache.Set if TTL is ≤ 0.
findings.verification: Unit test: mock ExpiresAt.Unix() == now.Unix() + 0.5; verify getCacheExpirationDuration returns 0 (not DefaultExpiration).
traceability: CWE-613: Insufficient Session Expiration

triage.reason: Timing is deterministic but the boundary (current second) is attacker-influenced via token issuance timing.

findings.inference: Assumes the test suite does not cover the boundary case (ExpiresAt == now); if it does, the behavior might be intentional.
findings.what_would_settle_it: Examination of jwtcache_test.go to see if it tests the boundary (now ± 1 second). If no boundary tests exist, this is a gap.

findings.title: Full bearer JWTs and IdP payloads logged at default level (CWE-532)
findings.evidence: Lines 235, 243, 249: complete JWT logged. openid.go:52, adfs.go:107, azure.go:92, and 8 others: full userinfo JSON logged at Info level (default). Email, phone_number, ou_name for Alibaba (structs.go:212-220) all exposed.
findings.impact: Credential leakage. Anyone with log access (SIEM, sidecar, aggregation vendor) can impersonate users with the full JWT lifetime (default 240 min).
findings.preconditions: Default log level (Info) enabled; logs are centralized or accessible.
findings.recommendation: Demote all provider Info dumps to Debug. Log token length or fingerprint instead of full payload. Use redaction filters on the JWT regex pattern.
findings.verification: Deploy with logLevel: info; send a login request; grep the logs for the full JWT or email; verify presence and that it is a valid token.
traceability: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

triage.reason: The JWT and userinfo are secrets; logging them is not essential.

findings.title: Unchecked type assertions on IdP responses cause remote panics (CWE-754)
findings.evidence: Lines 38–44, 63: json.Unmarshal into interface{} succeeds for null, leaving nil interface. Assertion f.(map[string]interface{}) panics. Reachable from every provider via MapClaims. A userinfo endpoint returning literal null crashes the auth request.
findings.impact: Denial of service. IdP outage or a network error returning null body causes Vouch to panic and abort the request.
findings.preconditions: Userinfo endpoint returns null or non-object JSON.
findings.recommendation: m, ok := f.(map[string]interface{}); if !ok { return fmt.Errorf(...) }.
findings.verification: Mock userinfo endpoint to return null; verify panic does not occur.
traceability: CWE-754: Improper Check for Unusual Conditions

triage.reason: IdP response is attacker-influenced (attacker controls their IdP response).

findings.title: GitHub org-membership check leaks response body and nil-deref panic (CWE-772, CWE-476)
findings.evidence: Lines 120–149: orgMembershipResp.Body never closed (no defer). Line 128-136: if Get on line 130 fails, no return, so line 139 nil-deref panics. Also: oauth2 transport injects Authorization header below http.Client's cross-host stripping, so manual 302 follow sends user's GitHub token to attacker-controlled Location.
findings.impact: Resource leak and denial of service (fd exhaustion, panic). SSRF via token leakage if IdP redirects to attacker host.
findings.preconditions: GitHub org check enabled; IdP returns 302; or org API is unreachable.
findings.recommendation: defer orgMembershipResp.Body.Close(); return false, err in inner error branch; validate Location matches UserOrgURL host.
findings.verification: Enable GitHub org check; mock org endpoint to return 302; verify panic does not occur and Body is closed.
traceability: CWE-772: Missing Release of Resource
CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference

triage.reason: Missing defer and missing return are clear bugs.

findings.title: No HTTP status code check on userinfo responses; 401/500 parsed as valid user (CWE-754)
findings.evidence: Nine provider implementations (openid.go:42-51, google.go:42-51, github.go, etc.) call io.ReadAll on userinfo.Body without checking userinfo.StatusCode. A 401/403/429/500 body is parsed as if it were a user record. Empty {} unmarshal to User{} yielding empty Username/Email.
findings.impact: Authorization bypass or denial of service. An IdP outage or token revocation returns an error body that gets parsed as an anonymous user, authorizing access.
findings.preconditions: IdP userinfo endpoint is misconfigured, overloaded, or the token is revoked.
findings.recommendation: if userinfo.StatusCode != http.StatusOK { return fmt.Errorf(...) } before parsing body. Also use io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(userinfo.Body, 1<<20)).
findings.verification: Mock userinfo endpoint to return 500 with error JSON; verify error is returned and user is not authorized.
traceability: CWE-754: Improper Check for Unusual Conditions

triage.reason: Missing status check is a clear bug.

findings.title: nginx examples never clear client-supplied X-Vouch-* headers (CWE-290)
findings.evidence: All nine nginx configs set proxy_set_header X-Vouch-User $auth_resp_x_vouch_user (correct); but they never clear X-Vouch-Success, X-Vouch-Error, X-Vouch-Token, X-Vouch-IdP-Claims-*, etc. nginx forwards unknown client headers by default. Attacker sends X-Vouch-Success: true and backend gates on it.
findings.impact: Authorization bypass. Backend author gates on X-Vouch-Success or X-Vouch-IdP-Claims-Groups (both plausible) — any authenticated user can send them and spoof authorization.
findings.preconditions: Backend trusts any X-Vouch-* header without verifying it came from Vouch.
findings.recommendation: Add proxy_set_header X-Vouch-Success ""; proxy_set_header X-Vouch-Error ""; proxy_set_header X-Vouch-Token ""; etc. to every example.
findings.verification: Send request with X-Vouch-Success: true directly to backend via nginx; verify backend rejects or does not gate on it.
traceability: CWE-290: Authentication Bypass by Spoofing

triage.reason: Exposure of /validate is not intended; clearing headers is standard nginx hardening.

findings.title: /validate is not marked internal; same-origin XSS steals IdP tokens (CWE-200)
findings.evidence: No nginx config example has location = /validate { internal; }. /validate is therefore publicly fetchable. handlers/validate.go:62-71 returns IdP access and ID tokens in response headers.
findings.impact: IdP account compromise via XSS escalation. An XSS on the protected app does fetch('/validate') same-origin (CORS does not apply) and reads the token.
findings.preconditions: XSS exists on the protected app; /validate is routed to the same origin.
findings.recommendation: Add location = /validate { internal; } to every nginx example. This tells nginx to refuse external requests.
findings.verification: curl https://protectedapp.example.com/validate without auth; verify 404 or rejection (if internal: is set) or 200 (if not set).
traceability: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

triage.reason: /validate is designed for Nginx only; external access is not intended.

findings.title: Weak jwt.secret and session.key only warned, never rejected (CWE-326)
findings.evidence: Lines 444-449 and 467-471 log.Errorf() if secrets are too short, then execution continues. A one-character HMAC secret starts successfully. Every other config error returns an error and triggers logger.Fatal (main.go:125-127); these two are exceptions.
findings.impact: Authentication bypass via weak secret. Forged JWTs mean full access across every site if the secret is too short.
findings.preconditions: Operator explicitly sets a very short secret; or auto-generation produces a short secret (unlikely, but not verified).
findings.recommendation: Return an error instead of log.Errorf so startup fails closed. Test auto-generation produces >= minBase64Length characters.
findings.verification: Set jwt.secret: a in config; verify startup fails (after fix) vs succeeds (before).
traceability: CWE-326: Inadequate Encryption Strength

triage.reason: Operator explicitly setting a short secret is an adversarial configuration.

ruled_out.where: Type assertion panics on session values (L-1), session cookie MaxAge ineffective (L-2), session cookie unsigned not encrypted (L-3), JWT in query string in logs (L-4), empty domain allow-list collapse (L-5), redirect-loop breaker inert (L-6), data race in timelog (L-7), raw JWT in HTML (L-8), SameSite=None without Secure (L-9), ClearCookie omits SameSite (L-10), TLS private key mode 0644 (L-11), unpinned base images (L-12), TLSConfig typo bypass (L-13), claim interpolation breaks JSON (L-14), plaintext HTTP in examples (L-15), secret in docker login script argv (L-16), ADFS unmarshal error ignored (L-17), GitHub URL injection (L-18), no rate limiting (L-19), test dependencies in production (L-20). All confirmed but grouped as LOW per severity scale: either defended by compensating control (L-8 has html/template), or narrow blast radius (L-11 local only), or operator error (L-4 querystring default should be off), or require attacker setup (L-14 needs IdP claims with JSON chars). All are listed in security-auditor's full audit output.

SameSite cookie default is 'None': actually http.SameSite(0) which is unset; browsers apply their own default (Lax). Open redirect via requestedURL: validated against domain allow-list before storage. AllowAllUsers bypasses domain check: unreachable; basicTest enforces domains XOR allowAllUsers. CSRF protection absent: present and correct via state nonce + PKCE.
